summary.text: Roger Williams is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 25th District. A former baseball player, small-business owner and Texas Secretary of State (2005–2007), he was first elected to Congress in 2012 and chairs the House Committee on Small Business. He is also a member of the Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Williams was born in Evanston, Illinois, in 1949, and raised in Fort Worth, Texas, according to Ballotpedia and his official biography.

He earned a bachelor's degree in education from Texas Christian University in 1972, and his official biography says he was an All-Southwest Conference baseball player at TCU. He played baseball in the Atlanta Braves farm system and then worked as a small business owner and baseball coach; his 2020 campaign website said he had been a small business owner in Texas for over 45 years.

Williams began his political involvement in 1994 as a fundraiser for then-Governor George W. Bush and was North Texas Finance Chairman for the 2000 Bush/Cheney presidential campaign, according to his official biography. His 2020 campaign website also said President Bush appointed him in 2001 as chairman of the Republican National Finance Committee's Eagles Program.
He served as Texas Secretary of State from 2005 to 2007, and his official biography says he also served as the state's chief liaison for the Texas border and Mexican affairs.

Williams was first elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and represents a district stretching from Tarrant County in the east to Callahan County in the west. He chairs the House Committee on Small Business and serves on the House Financial Services Committee.

His official biography lists bills he worked on that passed the House, including the Assisting Small Businesses Not Fraudsters Act, the Main Street Parity Act and the Strengthening Oversight of Iran's Access to Finance Act.

He serves on the TCU Board of Trustees, and his 2020 campaign website also listed service on the board of the Bush School of Government and Public Service at Texas A&M University. His official biography says he lives in Weatherford, Texas, and has two daughters and grandchildren.
